t: After defeat in the Second Opium War and amid the Taiping Rebellion, Qing officials set out to “strengthen themselves” by adopting Western arms, ships and industry while keeping the Confucian order.
Led above all by provincial governors such as Zeng Guofan, Li Hongzhang and Zuo Zongtang, it built arsenals, shipyards, mines, telegraphs, schools and a modern navy, and sent students abroad.
Without reform of government, finance or education its gains stayed scattered, and defeat by Japan in 1894–1895 exposed the limits of borrowing technology alone.
dyk: China’s first railway in regular service, from Shanghai to Wusong, was built by a British firm without the government’s consent and opened in 1876; the Qing authorities bought it in 1877 and had it torn up.
ev: The Zongli Yamen is created under Prince Gong to conduct relations with the Western powers
The Tongwen Guan opens in Beijing to train interpreters, later adding mathematics and astronomy
Zeng Guofan and Li Hongzhang found the Jiangnan Arsenal at Shanghai
Zuo Zongtang founds the Fuzhou Navy Yard and its naval school
The China Merchants’ Steam Navigation Company is founded; the first Educational Mission students sail for America
A French squadron destroys the Fujian fleet at Fuzhou in the Sino-French War
The Beiyang Fleet is formally established under Admiral Ding Ruchang
Defeated by Japan, the Qing sign the Treaty of Shimonoseki

f.where: Qing China: the court and the Zongli Yamen at Beijing, and the provincial governments of the lower Yangzi, Fujian, Zhili and Hubei, with arsenals and shipyards at Shanghai, Nanjing, Fuzhou and Tianjin
f.period: 1861–1895: from the creation of the Zongli Yamen after the Second Opium War to defeat by Japan; often divided into phases of arms and schools (1861–1872), enterprises for wealth (1872–1885) and industry and naval building (1885–1895)
f.figures: Prince Gong, Wenxiang, Zeng Guofan, Li Hongzhang, Zuo Zongtang, Zhang Zhidong
f.outcome: China’s first modern arsenals, shipyards, mines, telegraphs and technical schools and a modern navy, but no reform of institutions; defeat by Japan in 1894–1895 discredited it
